transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... well, I guess I came in because... I've been doing some things at work and school lately that, um, well, people say they don't make a lot of sense. It's really nothing too terrible, I promise! I just... I don't want to cause any trouble for my boss or my teachers. 

But I'll catch myself doing these little things, like... I'll start lining up all the work receipts across the floor instead of just entering them in the system. Or I'll find myself tapping my calculator in sets of nine. It just sort of happens, if that makes sense? And sometimes I guess I just stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air, just waiting there until someone asks if I'm okay. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly, and I'm really sorry if it's weird or if I'm wasting your time, but... is that the sort of thing I should be talking to you about? Am I explaining that okay?

When you find yourself doing these things, like lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator, do you feel like you have to do them to prevent something bad from happening or to stop yourself from feeling intense anxiety?

Oh, no, no, it's not like that at all. I don't feel scared or anxious or anything like that. I'm really sorry if I made it sound like I was panicking or something—I'm definitely not! 

It's just... I don't know, it just sort of feels like the right thing to do in the moment? Like, I don't think anything bad is going to happen if I don't tap the calculator or line up the receipts. It's just a little quirk, I guess. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way. Does that make sense?
When you are doing these things, like standing by the copier with your hands in the air, do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

Um... well... I guess, um, sometimes? But it's really nothing scary, I promise! I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything. 

It's just... sometimes when I'm all alone at my desk, or maybe walking home from class, I'll hear this guy's voice. He just says really normal things, like "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." It sounds so real and clear that I actually look around to see who's talking to me, but... nobody's ever there. 

It's just a little thing, though! It doesn't bother me too much. Is it... is it okay that I hear that sometimes? I'm answering your questions alright, aren't I?
When you are speaking to people at work or school, do they ever tell you that your sentences don't seem to connect or that it's difficult to follow your train of thought?

Um... well, sometimes? I really hope that's not a bad thing, though. I try my best to be clear, I really do! 

But, um, sometimes if I'm trying to explain something to my boss—like if a ledger is off or something—I guess my brain just sort of goes a little fast? Like, I'll start talking about the ledger, and then I'll think about my tuition deadlines, and then that reminds me of, um, tax rules, and then somehow I'm talking about studio lighting and the patterns in the numbers. 

And, um, my boss or my teachers will stop me and say they don't really get how I got from point A to point B. They say they can't follow my train of thought. 

It's just because I have a lot on my mind, I think! I'm really sorry if that sounds bad or if I'm not making sense right now. Am I explaining that okay for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have these patterns of speech or these behaviors you mentioned ever caused you to lose a job, leave school, or be unable to maintain close friendships?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? But I promise I'm really trying my best to keep everything on track! I hope you don't think I'm just slacking off or anything. 

It's just... recently, I did fail this one important course module for school. And, um, at work, some of my ledgers have been coming back with... well, some serious errors. I've actually had to start asking for help with things that used to be super routine for me, which is a little embarrassing to admit. 

But I'm working really hard to fix it, I swear! I just want to do a good job. Is it okay that I'm struggling a little right now? I hope that's not too bad of an answer. Am I giving you the information you need?
How long have you been experiencing these things, like hearing that voice or feeling the need to act in those specific ways?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever or anything! I'd say maybe... about 10 months? Give or take? 

It kind of started building up right around the time I began taking those evening accounting courses, you know, on top of keeping my regular bookkeeping job. It's just a lot to juggle, so I'm sure it's just stress from trying to do both at the same time. I mean, anyone would be a little overwhelmed, right? 

I really hope that doesn't make it sound like I can't handle my responsibilities. I'm usually really good at managing things! Is 10 months a bad answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline so you can help me.
When you are around other people, do you generally feel comfortable, or do you feel a sense of unease, suspicion, or a strong desire to avoid social interactions?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm suspicious of people or anything like that! I still really care about my friends and everyone. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm becoming some kind of hermit or pushing people away on purpose.

It's just... lately, I guess I've been a little less social? Like, I'll see a text from a friend and just sort of let it sit there unanswered for a while. And I've been skipping out on hanging out with people after my evening classes. 

Even when my friends are talking about stuff we usually love, like, um, going to music shows or talking about art projects, I just feel kind of... flat? Like I don't have the energy to get excited about it right now. 

But I promise I'm not trying to be rude to anyone! I just feel a little drained, maybe? Is it okay that I'm taking a little step back from socializing right now? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something completely wrong by needing some quiet time.
Do you ever feel like casual events, like something you see on the news or a billboard, contain a special, personal message specifically for you?

Um... well, not really things like the news or billboards, no! I know that would sound a little crazy, and I promise I'm not... I'm not thinking like that. 

But... well, I guess at work, sometimes... I don't know if this is what you mean, but sometimes I get this really strong feeling about the numbers. Like, um, certain invoice totals or account numbers, or even the due dates we put in the system? It's embarrassing to say out loud, but I get convinced they're... like, messages about me. 

My supervisor has actually sat down with me to show me that they're just normal entries, and I nod and agree because I don't want to cause trouble or seem difficult! But even after he explains it, I still have this lingering feeling that they're tracking me to see if I understand the pattern. 

I know it sounds so strange, and I'm really trying not to let it affect my work too much! I hope you don't think I'm losing my mind or anything. Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes, as long as I'm trying to ignore it?
When you feel like these numbers are tracking you or sending you messages, do you have a complex, detailed belief system or theory about who is sending them or why they are doing it?

Oh, um... no, definitely not a whole big theory! I really don't want to sound like I'm coming up with wild conspiracies or anything. 

Like I was just saying, it's really just that specific feeling about the invoice totals and account numbers. I don't really know who is behind it or why, exactly. It's just... even after my supervisor proves to me that they're completely normal entries, I just can't shake that conviction that the due dates and numbers are messages about me, tracking if I'm catching on to the pattern. 

But I don't have some big, complicated explanation for it! I just kind of... feel it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right, I just really don't want you to think I'm totally out of touch with reality or making things up.
Beyond the feelings about the numbers, do you feel like your range of emotions has become limited, or that it is difficult for you to express feelings like happiness or sadness as you used to?

Um, yeah, I think that's kind of what I was trying to explain earlier? I hope it's okay that I brought it up before you asked! But yes, like I mentioned, I really do still care about people... I don't want you to think I'm becoming cold or heartless or anything like that. 

It's just that most days lately, I end up letting my texts sit unanswered, and I'll skip hanging out after class. And when my friends bring up things I used to really enjoy, like those music shows or art projects... I just feel so flat. Like the happiness or excitement just doesn't surface the way it's supposed to? I try to act normal and smile so I don't bring everyone down, but it really is difficult to actually feel or express those emotions right now. 

Does that answer your question? I'm really trying to be honest about it, even though I feel a little guilty for not being more fun to be around. I hope I'm making sense!
